subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: For Telegram/ACP source turns that produce visible success-looking final text without matching tool or side-effect evidence, should OpenClaw add a narrow core diagnostic/retry contract, expose/extend plugin hooks only, or document that broad claim verification is out of core scope?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the safe behavior depends on maintainer intent around privacy, retry/fail-closed semantics, and the already-closed plugin-scope direction for generic claim verification.

options.title: Narrow source-channel contract
options.body: After live repro, define a small core Telegram/ACP finalization diagnostic or retry path that avoids leaking private finals and does not try to solve general NLP claim verification.

options.title: Plugin/API-only path
options.body: Keep core behavior as-is and track only any missing hook or delivery-evidence API needed for a ClawHub/community claim-verification plugin.

options.title: Broad core verification gate
options.body: Build a general ledger-backed success-claim verifier in core, accepting the product and maintenance cost of a policy engine.

recommendation.title: Narrow source-channel contract
recommendation.body: After live repro, define a small core Telegram/ACP finalization diagnostic or retry path that avoids leaking private finals and does not try to solve general NLP claim verification.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete made the related #68051 plugin-scope decision and is the clearest owner for the core-versus-plugin policy question here.
